header.reason: We won the online membership billing because our solutions engineer showed the controller which of Corelane's own failed renewals could be recovered. The signature followed four days after that session, once the contract had sat with him for two weeks. The front desks were not part of the deal and still run on Global Payments, and the rep first credited the head of digital rather than the controller who signed.

findings.label: What started it
findings.finding: Churn reported to the board rose two quarters running. Once it was split, failed cards turned out to be a bigger share than voluntary cancellations. In this deal, the moment to aim at was a finance or board review of churn, before anyone was thinking about payments vendors.
findings.quote: somebody finally split it into people who cancelled and people whose card just failed.

findings.label: Who decided
findings.finding: Maya, the head of digital and our champion, chose us. Greg, the controller, held the contract for two weeks and signed it, so he decided whether any switch happened at all. The rep only saw this when asked about it, which suggests we need a message for the finance gatekeeper as well as for the champion.
findings.quote: The paper had gone to Greg and it sat with him for two weeks.

findings.label: The competitor
findings.finding: According to Maya, the incumbent Global Payments came back with a rate review and a new front-desk terminal bundle on a longer contract; the rep never saw the offer, and the AE thinks they were rattled. After that meeting the questions moved from failed payments to readers, fit with the studio software and exit costs. This suggests the incumbent pulled the conversation onto hardware and lock-in, where it is strongest.
findings.quote: After it was, what readers do you have, do they work inside our studio software, what's the contract term, what does it cost to get out.

findings.label: Our message
findings.finding: Failed payment recovery landed when it was shown in the customer's own file. The global slide got silence from a business with US studios and a handful in Canada. 'Unified commerce' meant nothing until Maya turned it into a question about readers. For a mostly single-region customer, the global and unified commerce framing seems to have been noise.
findings.quote: Silence. I opened with the global slide.

findings.label: Missing proof
findings.finding: They asked to see our reader working inside their studio management software, on one screen at the front desk, and we couldn't show it live. They only saw a partner demo, not in their own setup. The studios are now phase two with no date, waiting on the partner piece, so this gap is what is holding back the rest of the account.
findings.quote: We couldn't show that live. It runs through a partner integration

findings.label: Their words
findings.finding: Maya called the problem 'members who never meant to leave', which is about churn and members. We call it failed payment recovery, which is about payments. The direct question about their words was pushed to Slack and never answered, so this rests on phrases the rep passed along.
findings.quote: members who never meant to leave.
